clue.text: Though service is good, citizen turns sort of acid

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve so good the receiver cannot touch it

indicators.note: the citizen word turns round, so its letters are read backwards here

parts.note: CIT is an old short form for a citizen or townsman

explanation.surface: A grumpy citizen sours even though the service he gets is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses CIT to give TIC, which follows ACE. 'Though' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the sour compound that gives vinegar its taste, so the word names a kind of acid.

clue.text: It would be material to study this island

definitions.text: It would be material to study this island

parts.words: It would be material to study this island
parts.note: add letters to the island's name and it becomes a printed cotton fabric, cretonne

explanation.surface: A remark that something is relevant to research on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like 'relevant'; it is cloth: with ON N set in, the island's name makes CRETONNE, a cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island's name lies inside the word for a heavy printed cotton fabric.

clue.text: You need a brainwave to explain this phenomenon

definitions.text: You need a brainwave to explain this phenomenon

parts.words: You need a brainwave to explain this phenomenon
parts.note: a brainwave here is a wave travelling from one mind to another, not a bright idea

explanation.surface: Only a flash of insight could account for something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brainwave' means a clever idea; read literally it is a mental signal sent between minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought transference is the supposed passing of thoughts from mind to mind without speech.

clue.text: No score in French cricket? What a rumour!

definitions.meaning: a batsman out for nothing makes a duck

explanation.surface: A rumour goes round that nobody scored in a game of French cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: French cricket is a real children's game, but here 'French' asks for the French word for the cricketer's duck (a score of nought).
explanation.definitionFit: A duck is a zero score in cricket, and the French word for duck also means an unfounded story.

clue.text: Refinements of Riviera neckwear

parts.note: Nice is the chief resort city of the French Riviera
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Fashionable people on the Côte d'Azur show their refinement in the ties they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Small points of etiquette or delicate distinctions are subtleties of manner.

clue.text: Offering no resistance, all the same

definitions.meaning: split as ..., not holding out against something

explanation.surface: Someone who gives in but carries on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nevertheless, and split in two it means not holding out against.

clue.text: Learn lines for speaking

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
verse is written in lines

explanation.surface: An actor memorises lines in order to speak them.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun sense is meant: converse is talk, conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Converse as a noun means conversation, talk between people.

clue.text: Identity sought by jesting Pilate

parts.note: recalls Bacon's line 'What is ...? said jesting Pilate, and would not stay for an answer'

explanation.surface: Pontius Pilate mockingly asks who someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon's essay opens 'What is truth? said jesting Pilate'. 'Identity' is used in its sense of what a thing really is, agreement with fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilate's famous question to Jesus asked what is real and factual.

clue.text: Borne shoulder-high by old soldier on promotion

definitions.text: Borne shoulder-high by old soldier on promotion

parts.words: Borne shoulder-high by old soldier on promotion
parts.note: not a soldier carried aloft in triumph, but the ornamental shoulder piece worn as a mark of rank

explanation.surface: A veteran is hoisted onto shoulders when promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borne shoulder-high' suggests a triumphant carry; it is the fringed pad worn on the shoulder, gained by officers on promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers wear an ornamental shoulder piece showing their rank.

clue.text: Duke of Somerset ?

parts.note: read as a title: a famous duke whose title is taken from a small town in the county of Somerset

explanation.surface: A query about which nobleman holds the Somerset dukedom.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a real Duke of Somerset, so the clue looks like a peerage question; the answer is the duke whose title came from a Somerset town, the victor of Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley, the Iron Duke, took his title from a market town in Somerset.

clue.text: Eastwood had up as poisoner

indicators.note: the words that follow hold the answer, so 'had' says they contain it

explanation.surface: Clint Eastwood once had someone held up as a poisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastwood' describes the answer too: it is a tree of the East (Java), whose sap was used on poison darts, and the letters of 'up as' give it outright.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas tree of Java yields a toxic sap and was fabled to kill anything near it.

clue.text: Poet spotted animal — I follow

indicators.note: I comes after the animal, so 'follow' places it at the end

parts.note: the leopard is the big cat known for its spots

explanation.surface: A poet watches a spotted big cat and trails after it.
explanation.walkthrough: Giacomo Leopardi was a 19th-century Italian lyric poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Leopardi was a celebrated Italian writer of verse.

clue.text: Get out of breath, being no longer fit

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
hale means healthy and fit

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost fitness ends up breathless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out of breath' looks like 'become breathless'; it means send breath out.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out is to expel air from the lungs.

clue.text: Revolver used by 'Cook

parts.note: read not as a gun but as a turning rod that a kitchen cook roasts meat on

explanation.surface: A pistol used by someone called Cook, perhaps the explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a handgun and 'Cook' a name such as Captain Cook; it is a rotating skewer for roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting skewer turns meat over the fire, so it is a rotating device in the kitchen.

clue.text: One of a number to delay splash-down

definitions.text: One of a number to delay splash-down

parts.words: One of a number to delay splash-down
parts.note: a space capsule falls to the sea under several canopies that slow its descent

explanation.surface: A space capsule's return to the sea is slowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Returning space capsules of the era came down in the sea under a cluster of canopies.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy that slows a fall through the air; capsules used several to land at sea.

clue.text: Proverbial way to get lost

parts.note: points to the saying that whoever wavers is lost

explanation.surface: A well-known way of losing one's way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get lost' suggests losing direction; the proverb is 'He who hesitates is lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the person who pauses in doubt is lost, so wavering is the route to loss.

clue.text: Scold or nag: matter for putting straight

indicators.note: putting straight means sorting out, so the letters of nag and matter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scold or nag needs something to put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting straight' rearranges NAG and MATTER. 'or' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Woo painter I find in Belgium

parts.note: to court is to woo
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A suitor and an artist meet in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: Courtrai is the French name of Kortrijk, a Flemish city. 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtrai, or Kortrijk, is a city in Flanders in the west of the country.

clue.text: John Peel the Confederate?

definitions.meaning: the hunting song says John Peel had a coat so grey
Confederate soldiers in the American Civil War wore grey uniforms

explanation.surface: A huntsman of song mistaken for a Southern rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel is the Cumbrian huntsman of the song 'D'ye ken John Peel', 'with his coat so grey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the famous huntsman and the Southern soldier were known by the grey garment they wore.

clue.text: What became of Pan's nymph ?

parts.note: recalls the myth of Syrinx, the nymph Pan chased, who was changed into a marsh plant

explanation.surface: A question about the fate of the nymph the god Pan loved.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrinx escaped Pan by turning into marsh plants, from which he cut his pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrinx was transformed into the tall marsh plant from which Pan made his pipes.

clue.text: Packs before mounting

parts.note: read as what a taxidermist does to a specimen before setting it on display

explanation.surface: A traveller packs his bags before getting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' suggests climbing into the saddle; it is a taxidermist mounting a specimen, which he first fills.
explanation.definitionFit: Fills, crams, and also what the taxidermist does to an animal skin before display.

clue.text: Crystal gazer is learning to take old port? Right

indicators.note: the learning word takes the port after it, so the two pieces join

parts.note: Sc is the abbreviation for science, learning as in BSc
Rye in Sussex was one of the old Cinque Ports, now silted up

explanation.surface: A fortune teller is learning to drink port, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old port' suggests a vintage drink; it is RYE, a former Cinque Port. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scryer foretells the future by looking into a crystal ball or mirror.

clue.text: The story of Kingsley caused a ferment

definitions.text: The story of Kingsley caused a ferment

parts.words: The story of Kingsley caused a ferment
parts.note: Charles Kingsley wrote a novel named after the agent that makes dough rise and beer ferment

explanation.surface: A novel by Kingsley stirred up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Kingsley's 1848 novel 'Yeast' did stir controversy; the ferment is also literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus that causes fermentation also gave its name to a Kingsley novel.

clue.text: Result of incubation by a hazel-hen ?

definitions.text: Result of incubation by a hazel-hen ?

parts.words: Result of incubation by a hazel-hen ?
parts.note: read playfully: a hazel nut that has been sat on until it hatches, giving a small bird

explanation.surface: What comes from the eggs a grouse-like bird sits on.
explanation.walkthrough: A hazel-hen is a real grouse, so the clue seems to ask about its chick; read 'hazel' as a nut and the hatching gives the small tree-climbing bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut that hatches would be a nut hatch, the name of the small woodland bird.

clue.text: Transparent net

definitions.meaning: as in net profit, what remains after deductions

explanation.surface: A see-through mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass is see-through, and a profit after deductions is one made with nothing owing.

clue.text: He backs up Mum, the beast

indicators.note: the word up goes backwards, so 'backs' turns it round

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A man stands by his mother against a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reverses UP to PU, then MA follows. 'He' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a large American wild cat, also called the cougar.

clue.text: Given fresh air after a collapse

definitions.text: Given fresh air after a collapse

parts.words: Given fresh air after a collapse
parts.note: read not as a person revived but as a tyre or balloon pumped up again after going flat

explanation.surface: Someone who fainted is taken outside to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests first aid for someone who has collapsed; it describes something deflated being pumped up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumping air into something that has gone flat blows it up once more.

clue.text: Like the entomologist's brows ?

parts.note: an insect expert might be busy hunting insects, and the word for that also means overhanging

explanation.surface: A description of an insect scientist's eyebrows.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetling brows are shaggy and overhanging; an entomologist would also be out after beetles.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhanging, jutting brows are called beetling, and an insect collector goes after beetles.

clue.text: They're only half qualified to play the goat

definitions.text: They're only half qualified to play the goat

parts.words: They're only half qualified to play the goat
parts.note: creatures of myth that are half goat and half man, so only half suited to the part

explanation.surface: Actors with only half the credentials to fool about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play the goat' means act the fool; these woodland spirits of Greek myth have goat's legs and human bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs in Greek myth have goat legs and horns on a human body, so they are only half goat.
